A Small Argument for Going Back

Sometimes a second viewing is less repetition than discovery.

By Steve Berkowitz August 4, 2026 About 3 minutes
Attention

The first viewing often belongs to plot. The second belongs to everything else.

A gesture that seemed incidental becomes the scene. A cut that felt invisible suddenly carries the emotion. Rewatching is not always about comfort; sometimes it is the first time we properly notice what a film is doing.

—

Thank you for reading.
